data.title: Sky Founder Says Protocol Is Operating Normally as Committee Launches 5.25 Million USDS Buyback
data.description:
Sky Protocol founder Rune Christensen said the protocol is operating normally and financially sound, while Sky’s core committee announced a one-time 5.25 million USDS buyback. According to Odaily, Christensen said recent reports about Sky were overstated, USDS remains overcollateralized with about $10 billion in asset backing, and the protocol’s mechanisms are working as designed.

Sky processed more than $2 billion in outflows over the past 24 hours, Christensen said. Liquidity supporting the stablecoin’s peg remained above $2 billion and has since risen to more than $2.25 billion. Sky generated about $400 million in revenue over the past year.

The buyback will follow the process set out in Sky Atlas, with 750,000 USDS allocated each day for seven consecutive days, for a total of 5.25 million USDS.

data.title: Tom Lee Says Selling the S&P 500 Amid Rising Pessimism Could Mean Selling at the Bottom
data.description:
According to ChainCatcher, Bitmine Chairman Tom Lee said worsening market pessimism may make selling now tantamount to selling at the bottom. He said the market decline reflects investors reducing risk exposure amid multiple concerns rather than deteriorating fundamentals.

Over the past 15 years, the S&P 500 rose in the week after six consecutive trading-day declines in all 10 observed cases, gaining an average of 2.7% and a median of 2.1%. Lee also put the probability of the index rising Friday at 70%.

data.title: Japan Pension Fund Proxy Banks Become Net Sellers of JGBs for First Time Since April 2025
data.description: According to Sina Finance, citing the Japan Securities Dealers Association, trust banks acting as pension fund agents net sold 92.6 billion yen of Japanese government bonds in October, the first net selling since April 2025. They sold 522.4 billion yen of 10-year bonds, more than their net purchases of medium- and super-long-term bonds. Commercial banks were net sellers for a second consecutive month, their longest selling streak since May 2025.

data.title: Anthropic Perpetual Contracts on Hyperliquid Record $1.85 Billion in Volume Across Three Markets
data.description: Anthropic (ANT) perpetual contracts on Hyperliquid recorded $1.85 billion in trading volume across three markets, with open interest near $400 million. According to Odaily, TradeXYZ accounted for $1.67 billion in volume, more than 90% of the total.

data.title: Thailand Opens Market to US Pork, Adding Strain on Farmers
data.description: Thailand opened its pork market to US competition in trade negotiations, crossing a former red line and adding pressure on a domestic industry already facing excess supply and weak prices, according to Bloomberg.

data.title: IMF Chief Georgieva: AI Asset Correction May Not Be Over; Circular Financing Risks Financial Stability
data.description:
According to Sina Finance, IMF Managing Director Kristalina Georgieva said AI-related financial assets may face further corrections after market enthusiasm became excessive, and warned that circular financing could pose risks to financial stability.

In an interview with the media in Shenzhen on Thursday, Georgieva said the IMF had anticipated a market correction but had not yet seen a sharp one. Further adjustments could help return markets to a more sustainable state.

Concerns about whether massive AI investments will generate commensurate returns have recently added to global market volatility. On Thursday, Anthropic shares rose 17% above their offering price on their first day of trading, while the tech-heavy Nasdaq 100 fell 2.2%, as investors remained cautious about AI-related trades.

Georgieva put circular financing at about $1 trillion, with roughly two-thirds funded by debt. The term refers to chipmakers such as Nvidia providing financing to customers to help them buy the companies’ own equipment. She said the size was not in itself huge, but expressed concern about how quickly it was growing and the shift in financing from equity toward more debt.

She said greater transparency around these transactions and warnings to companies about entering riskier territory could help reduce the potential financial stability risks.

data.title: Japan Tobacco Shares Drop Following Russia-Related Charges
data.description: According to Bloomberg, Japan Tobacco Inc. shares declined after the cigarette maker said it expects to swing to an operating loss and cut its dividend forecast after losing control of its Russian business.

data.title: STOCKS | Nvidia Loses More Than 4.4 Trillion Yuan in Market Value Over Six Trading Days
data.description:
According to Sina Finance, citing Cailian Press, Nvidia shares fell 3.3% on Thursday to $145.98, extending their losing streak to six trading days. The stock fell 16% over the period, wiping $669 billion from the company's market value, or about 4.48 trillion yuan. Shares opened higher amid optimism surrounding Anthropic's initial public offering but closed lower.

Iskandar Rakhmatov, a portfolio manager at quantitative strategy research platform Zeus Quanto, said he believed the decline was not over. He cited Moody's move on Wednesday to change Nvidia's credit outlook from positive to stable, while noting that this was not a credit-rating downgrade and did not call the company's ability to repay debt into question. Rakhmatov said uncertainty over the CEO position and a board investigation were also weighing on the shares. Last week, CEO Jensen Huang announced his resignation amid rumors, and the board appointed Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress as interim CEO.

Shay Boloor, chief market strategist at Futurum Equities, said growth and AI stocks were undergoing one of the most aggressive de-risking moves in recent years. Nvidia shares fell despite the company reporting strong results for its previous fiscal quarter on Tuesday and raising its full-year guidance. Boloor said there was little evidence that demand for computing power was slowing and pointed to rising GPU rental prices.

Michael Casper, a senior market strategist at HB Wealth, said Nvidia had repeatedly peaked around $150 between November 2024 and January 2025. He said traders might be looking to buy near that level, but a break below it could prompt further selling. Nvidia closed below $150 on Thursday. Sentara Capital founder Will Allen said $148.80, the low during panic selling last Thursday morning after Huang announced his resignation, was an important near-term support level.

data.title: STOCKS | South Korea’s KOSPI Falls 4.1% as Anthropic IPO Fails to Ease Market Concerns
data.description:
According to Sina Finance, South Korea’s benchmark KOSPI index fell as much as 4.1%, as Anthropic’s large initial public offering failed to ease broad concerns about the sustainability of the global AI trade. Kyle Rodda, a senior financial markets analyst at Capital.com, said the IPO was not enough to allay investor concerns about the outlook for AI-related trading or the broader stock market.

Rodda said negative sentiment reflected persistent worries about a slowdown in AI investment and growth, as well as the possibility that the Federal Reserve could soon raise interest rates sharply, although the implied probability of such action edged down during U.S. trading. He said the boost from Anthropic’s listing was barely evident in Asian markets, where a cooling AI trade and the risk of aggressive Fed rate hikes tightening financial conditions had weighed on markets.

SK Hynix, a memory-chip maker, fell as much as 6.5%, while Samsung Electronics declined 4.8%. Japan’s Nikkei 225 also fell 3%.

data.title: GfK Survey Finds UK Consumers More Willing to Spend
data.description: British consumers showed a renewed appetite for spending on items such as furniture and electronics in November, according to a GfK survey, Bloomberg reported.

data.title: Colombia's National Digital Agency Reportedly Hacked, Data Exposed
data.description:
According to ChainCatcher, threat actor “BenjaminUSA” claimed to have obtained sensitive data from Colombia’s National Digital Agency (Agencia Nacional Digital, AND), which handles government digital services and technology. The alleged exposed information includes administrator usernames and password hashes, government email addresses, user account and profile records, and material related to internal dashboards and database access. The actor posted database excerpts and screenshots as purported evidence.

However, some screenshots show generic World Bank dashboard data. The alleged breach and its scope remain unclear, and the claims have not been verified.

data.title: Nous Research and Microsoft Launch Hermes Enterprise for Workplace Tasks
data.description:
According to ChainCatcher, Nous Research and Microsoft have partnered to bring Hermes Agent to enterprise users through Hermes Enterprise, available on Microsoft Teams, Microsoft Store, and Azure. Employees can assign tasks such as financial analysis, document drafting, and inbox organization in Teams and view results in the same chat. Agent tasks run in isolated Azure Container Apps sandboxes.

Hermes can save effective approaches from recurring tasks as skills, which employees can share with team members after review through Collective Wisdom. Enterprises with data residency or procurement requirements can deploy Hermes Enterprise in their own Azure tenants. Nous Research CTO Jeffrey Quesnelle discussed Hermes’ use of sandboxes at the BRK448 session at Microsoft Ignite.

data.title: Asian Currency Losers Rebound as Oil Retreats and AI Exposure Shrinks
data.description: A trade that drove Asian currencies for much of this year is starting to turn as oil prices retreat and investors slash exposure to the artificial-intelligence trade, according to Bloomberg.

data.title: Samsung Names Separate Memory and Mobile Heads, Keeps Co-CEO Lineup Unchanged
data.description: According to Sina Finance, Samsung Electronics appointed new heads of its memory and mobile businesses under co-CEOs Jun Young-hyun and TM Roh, according to an email statement from the company. Sang Joon Hwang was promoted to president and named head of the memory business, while Won-Joon Choi was appointed head of the mobile business. Jun will continue to lead the Device Solutions (DS) division, and Roh will continue to head the Device eXperience (DX) division; both will retain their co-CEO responsibilities.

data.title: Philadelphia Fed President Anna Paulson: Wage Growth Matches 2% Inflation, a Good Sign
data.description: According to Jin10, Philadelphia Fed President Anna Paulson said wage growth is consistent with 2% inflation, calling it a good sign.

data.title: KPMG Canada Reports Unauthorized Access to Clients’ Tax Files
data.description: According to ChainCatcher, KPMG Canada confirmed a cybersecurity incident in which an unauthorized third party accessed some clients’ tax files. The company said it acted immediately to contain the incident and secure its systems, and is contacting affected clients. Spokesperson Sonja Cloutier-Bosworth said KPMG is confident the data was not published online or used for other purposes. The company did not disclose how many clients were affected or how the access occurred.

data.title: Nintendo ADRs Jump After Roaring Kitty Account Posts Mario Image on X
data.description: According to Bloomberg, Nintendo Co.’s American depositary receipts soared Thursday after an account associated with Keith Gill, known online as “Roaring Kitty,” posted an image of the company’s mascot on X.

data.description: According to Sina Finance, SK Hynix shares fell 5.8% to 1,114,000 won in morning trading, while Samsung Electronics shares fell 4.3% to 188,400 won.
